controls: searchable local asset, character, and motion catalogs
editable lights, fog, and panorama environment lighting
film-language framing: intent-driven camera placement, camera-move marks, and geometric move naming
editable orbit, wave, and bounce animation recipes
ComfyUI image, video, sound-effect, music, and speech generation with Gallery promotion
durable audio/video transcription with adaptive long-media chunking, timed transcript search, JSON/VTT, and timeline caption promotion
capture-to-scene reconstruction: RGB-D scan bundles or RGB video into metric walls, swinging doors, proxy objects, capture-view cameras, and render-and-compare scoring
parameterized reusable macros and explicit untrusted memory
batch transforms, custom pivots, persistent annotations and measurements, ordered layers, isolation, focus framing, grouping, and clipping planes
living world ambient systems: seeded wind/weather/time-of-day settings, emitter effects, shader water bodies, and wildlife groups
drivable vehicle profiles consumed by live player sessions
recommended_loop: catalog when an asset or motion id is unknown
observe for a compact scene summary
observe with since_revision when only persisted changes are needed
query_objects when a name, kind, camera frustum, or local area is needed
check the changed entities or frame once

author_evidence_contract.request: Set author.evidence={} to request one clean camera frame after the author transaction commits. Use describe target author.evidence for optional fields; boolean true is invalid.
author_evidence_contract.default: camera_frame at 640x360 using evidence.camera_id, author.camera_id, or the active camera in that order.
author_evidence_contract.revision: The frame is captured against the exact committed project_revision. Capture failure is reported under result.evidence without misreporting the already-committed mutation as failed.
author_evidence_contract.attachment: Image bytes use the existing tool image attachment; result.evidence contains metadata only.

ui_observation_contract.request: Use observe with fields=[ui] for one current interaction-state snapshot.
ui_observation_contract.contract: Returns selection, active camera, transform mode, viewport layout, exact transient playhead frame, and selected timeline track/keyframe together.
ui_observation_contract.revision: UI observation is read-only and is intentionally excluded from project revision deltas.

harness_scheduling_contract.execution: Consecutive read-only tools may share one bounded parallel window. Across providers and sessions, calls bound to the same exact Director target share one Gateway reader/writer queue, and every mutation is an exclusive ordering barrier.
harness_scheduling_contract.cancellation: A request cancelled while waiting for its target lease is removed before browser dispatch.
harness_scheduling_contract.telemetry: Each hosted Harness tool.completed event includes harnessQueueWaitMs, targetQueueWaitMs, their combined queueWaitMs, executionMs excluding queue waits, elapsedMs, windowSize, and concurrencyLimit.

production_contract.concurrency: Pass expected_revision when a caller needs to reject edits made against an older production snapshot.
production_contract.activation: Scene activation is acknowledged by the manifest before the browser opens the scoped DirectorProject.
production_contract.duplication: The source scene must be loaded in the targeted browser. Director clones its validated project into an independent destination scope.
production_contract.deletion: Deleting the last scene requires an explicit replacement scene so the production remains openable.

generated_3d_contract.source_image: image-to-3d resolves source_media_id from the durable Gallery; binary image data never crosses the Agent tool wire.
generated_3d_contract.submission: Submit/retry are durable idempotent jobs. The public Agent boundary assigns a stable retry key when the caller omits one.
generated_3d_contract.promotion: promote imports a completed model and thumbnail into Gallery and applies one guarded, idempotent Stage asset/object mutation.
generated_3d_contract.normalization: Promoted GLB is meter/Y-up/right-handed, horizontally centered, grounded at Y=0, scaled to target_height_m, and retains exact provider provenance; target_height_m is optional and the gateway estimates a real-world height from the prompt when it is omitted, falling back to 1 m.

generation_contract.discovery: Discover live nodes and imported workflows before submission; workflow discovery returns bounded metadata rather than the full graph.
generation_contract.submission: Submit/retry are durable idempotent jobs. The public Agent boundary assigns a stable retry key when the caller omits one.
generation_contract.promotion: Only completed jobs may be promoted. Audio and video media generate waveform data when requested.
generation_contract.provenance: Promoted media retains its prompt, seed, node, workflow, parameters, provider job and source information.

transcription_contract.source: submit resolves an exact durable Gallery audio/video source_media_id in the bound browser; raw bytes never cross the Agent tool wire
transcription_contract.durability: The gateway records transcription as a production job that can be inspected after a browser refresh and adaptively chunks long media into bounded parallel provider requests.
transcription_contract.artifacts: Completed jobs publish transcript JSON and WebVTT artifacts.
transcription_contract.promotion: promote persists the transcript on the selected Gallery media and can add timed text clips to Video Editor.
transcription_contract.retrieval: read returns a bounded time window; search ranks matching timed segments and can filter by speaker and source time without sending the full transcript through the Agent wire.

automation_contract.macros: Named parameterized action templates are checked when saved and run as one undoable authoring mutation. Saving the same stable ID and content or removing an already absent macro is retry-safe.
automation_contract.memory: Memory is explicit local user data with pin, recall, forget and export actions. It is inserted into a prompt only when the user chooses it. Pinning the same stable ID and content or forgetting an already absent memory is retry-safe.

advanced_editor_contract.contract: Human and Agent surfaces compile advanced edits into ordinary persisted project fields and editable frame keyframes; annotations and measurements use object-local or world anchors, focus_objects frames exact IDs, layer state is effective without destroying per-object flags, one operation owns one undo snapshot, and locks require explicit force.

storyboard_artifact_contract.capture: Captures each storyboard shot at its selected camera and start frame and saves the thumbnail in Gallery.
storyboard_artifact_contract.concurrency: The public Agent boundary binds capture and export to the exact current project revision and assigns a stable retry key; the browser rejects unguarded execution.
storyboard_artifact_contract.export: export_pdf supports A4/Letter, portrait/landscape, 1-4 columns, all/selected scope, metadata and action notes.
storyboard_artifact_contract.download: The command can trigger the PDF or package download in the browser.

compare_contract.sources: reference and candidate each name one image endpoint: a live stage render (camera_id/frame/width/height, active camera when camera_id is omitted), a durable Gallery still (media_id), or a reconstruction capture keyframe (job_id with optional view_id/camera_id). candidate defaults to a stage render through the active camera. Image bytes stay in the bound browser; only scores and grid cells cross the Agent wire.
compare_contract.scoring: One shared luminance-grid scorer produces ssim, luminanceSimilarity, edgeSimilarity, and a weighted composite in 0..1; composite >= 0.75 reads as a strong match.
compare_contract.localization: grid.worst lists the weakest cells ordered worst-first, each with a normalized region rectangle (x0/y0/x1/y1 in 0..1 of the frame) so a caller can fix only those regions instead of rebuilding the scene.
compare_contract.loop: Quantify with score.composite, locate with grid.worst regions, fix only those regions (large forms and layout, then materials, then lighting), then compare again to verify.
compare_contract.relationship: reconstruction.compare is the plan-bound specialization of this operation: it resolves the capture-view camera from a reconstruction plan and scores through the same shared scorer.
compare_contract.routing: A comparison with a stage endpoint routes only to capture-ready Stage tabs; pure media/keyframe comparisons run on any bound browser tab.

shot_package_contract.passes: Helper-free PNG passes include clean, clay, albedo, roughness, metalness, emissive, ao, shadow, packed depth, normal, object-id, mask, pose, lineart, semantic, and motion. The depth pass additionally supports a metric float32 OpenEXR artifact.
shot_package_contract.include_depth_exr: Set include_depth_exr:true together with the depth render pass to add passes/depth/frame-XXXXXX.exr — a single FLOAT Z channel storing linear eye-space depth in scene metres with a far-plane background — plus depthSemantics metadata in the package manifest and an ai/control.json inputs.depthExr reference. The 8-bit depth PNG is still produced and existing packages stay byte-identical when the option is off.
shot_package_contract.handler_requirement: Requires a mounted Stage viewport whose capture handler supports float depth readback; older handlers fail with an explicit error instead of silently omitting the artifact.

spatial_contract.whitebox_authoring: White-box is a clay look, not a box kit. Instance catalog or project meshes, or model missing architecture in blender_native. Stage primitives are temporary massing markers only — never windows, doors, facades, furniture, characters, or trees.
spatial_contract.units: Director world units (1 unit = 1 metre for authored white-box geometry)
spatial_contract.primitive_pivot: Bottom centre, not geometric centre. position.y is the visible bottom. Grounded objects use position.y = scene.groundHeight. Do not use primitives as windows, doors, or facades.
spatial_contract.clearance: When explicit centre distance/spacing is omitted, place_relative, arrange_group, and arrange_facing_pair derive deterministic clearance from the shared rotated object bounds. Use clearance_m for an edge gap; do not combine it with distance_m/spacing_m.
placement_decision_order: Rests on another grounded/supported object -> supported; geometry must physically contact the support chain.
Mounted to the side/surface of a wall, vehicle, rig, or other spatially resolved object -> attached with parent_id.
Hangs from a spatially overhead resolved object -> suspended with parent_id.
Has deliberately no support because the artistic intent is airborne -> floating.

placement_semantics.auto: Legacy or intent-unknown placement. Audit still infers ground/support from bounds. If an elevated auto object is reported unsupported, inspect and classify it before correction; never blindly lower it.
placement_semantics.grounded: The visible bottom must meet scene.groundHeight. Primitive position.y is already the floor pivot; never add half of scale.y. Walls, columns, and furniture sit at y=0 (or scene.groundHeight), not at mid-height.
placement_semantics.supported: For shelf, table, stack, and platform contact. It requires physical top/overlap contact with an anchored support chain; parent_id alone is not support proof.
placement_semantics.attached: For wall-, vehicle-, rig-, or surface-mounted details. parent_id is required and must name an existing spatially resolved anchor. Inspect pixels for a plausible joint or contact.
placement_semantics.suspended: For chandeliers, hanging signs, cables, or props suspended from above. parent_id is required, must already resolve in the placement chain, and must be spatially overhead.
placement_semantics.floating: Only for intentional unsupported airborne props/effects such as a magic orb or VFX element. Never use it to silence a mistaken height, missing support, or hanging fixture.

parent_contract.semantic_role: parent_id declares an attachment/suspension anchor; it is not a look target and does not prove physical support for auto/supported placement.
parent_contract.anchor_requirement: Attached/suspended parents must already resolve in the placement chain; suspended also requires the parent footprint to be spatially overhead.
parent_contract.visual_requirement: Attachment/suspension semantics can pass coarse bounds checks, so deliver's clean frame must still be inspected for gaps, penetration, and implausible mounting.

spatial_contract.semantic_blocking: compose_blocking compiles facing/side-by-side/line/behind/circle layouts into grounded metric transforms, verified look targets, and a fitted active camera

composable_relations.contract: Use these actions to refine existing objects without rebuilding the scene. Screen left/right and foreground/background require camera reference; character-facing intent is persisted as look_target_object_id when a real target object exists.

object_queries.contract: Returns stable object IDs, canonical world bounds, distance, truncation metadata, and the current project revision without dumping the whole scene. Provide spatial, name_pattern, or kind. A camera query uses spatial {mode: frustum, camera_id?: id}, not a nested frustum object. name_pattern is a case-insensitive substring of object name or id. Set max_results from 1 to 200 when a bound is required; the default is 50.

observation_deltas.request: Pass observe.since_revision with optional fields and max_changes.
observation_deltas.contract: Returns only persisted project changes retained by the bounded workbench history. Each changed collection reports total_changes and truncation; UI state is intentionally excluded because it is not identified by project revision.

object_hierarchy.request: Pass observe.object_mode=hierarchy with fields=[objects] and optional max_objects.
object_hierarchy.contract: Returns stable nested parent-child nodes with total_count, returned_count, and truncation metadata instead of an unbounded flat object table.

procedural_authoring.contract: Every operation is bounded and deterministic; seeded operations persist the exact recipe and output IDs. fragment-scaffold and primitive terrain/L-system results are explicit blocking approximations, not production boolean meshes.

framing_contract.framing: frame_shot aims an existing camera at a subject object from crew vocabulary (size/view/side/level/lens) and reports the derived slate in the result notes. A physically impossible request lengthens the lens along the prime ladder or flattens the level and says so instead of failing silently.
framing_contract.moves_contract: mark_camera_move pins the camera's current framing (rig transform, aim, fov) as one keyframe on the camera's own animation track; a move is authored by framing twice and marking twice. describe_camera_move names the move the marked track geometrically proves between two frames and returns a prompt-ready phrase plus per-segment slates.
framing_contract.shared_language: The same film-language module derives shot vocabulary for the Stage HUD, observe, audit, and generation prompts, so UI and agents cannot disagree about what a framing is.

world_contract.determinism: World visuals are a pure function of (settings.seed, entry seedOffset, timeline time); authoring never stores wall-clock simulation state.
world_contract.creation: The first world authoring action creates project.world with default settings (enabled: true) on demand and reports that in the result notes.
world_contract.settings_merge: set_world_settings deep-merges partial snake_case wind/time_of_day/weather patches into the existing settings without clobbering sibling fields.
world_contract.weather_evolution: weather.evolution {mode: static|cycle, period_seconds 60..3600 (default 300)} turns the five presets into a seeded state machine: cycle ramps the climate vector (cloud cover, precipitation, wind gain) between preset nodes and integrates weather.wetness over world time, all a pure function of (seed, worldSeconds). Absent or static preserves the authored values verbatim. evolution: null removes the block.
world_contract.fire_propagation: Fire effects accept propagation {enabled, radius_m 2..64 (default 12), spread_rate 0.1..3 (default 1)}: a deterministic ground-grid burn that spreads with wind, is suppressed by wetness/rain, and never crosses authored water rectangles. Requires kind "fire" and an unbound anchor (anchor.object_id null). propagation: null removes it.
world_contract.anchoring: Effect anchor.object_id must reference an existing object; a null/absent object_id is a world-space anchor at anchor.position.
world_contract.roads: add_world_road sweeps a Catmull-Rom centerline through points (2..64 vec3s, Y carries road height); defaults width_m 8, vehicle_count 6, speed_kph 40, show_surface true, and loop is inferred when the first and last points coincide. Two-way instanced traffic is stateless in time: vehicle poses are a pure function of (seed, worldSeconds), open roads respawn vehicles at their start.
world_contract.locking: Locked world entries reject updates and removals until an update action unlocks them with patch {"locked": false}.

vehicle_contract.chassis_frame: Profile offsets use the chassis frame: forward +Z, up +Y, left +X; exit probes are tried in order with the left door first.
vehicle_contract.merge: set_vehicle_profile merges a partial snake_case profile onto the object's existing profile, or onto the default car profile when the object has none; an omitted or empty profile attaches pure defaults, and the result notes say whether it attached defaults or patched.
vehicle_contract.clearing: clear_vehicle_profile removes the capability and succeeds with an informative note when the object never had one.
vehicle_contract.locking: Locked objects reject vehicle profile writes and clears; only the standalone safety patch {"drivable": false} may disable an existing profile without an update_object {"locked": false} unlock first.
vehicle_contract.runtime: Vehicle profiles are live player-session capabilities (walk up, enter, drive, exit with a chase camera); they never affect deterministic timeline scrub, capture, or export.

camera_identity_contract.canonical_id: Use the id from observe.cameras for camera authoring and inspection.
camera_identity_contract.stage_projection_alias: Evidence operations also accept the linked camera-rig object id exposed by scene_hint/Stage projection and resolve it to the same exact Director camera; they never fall back to another camera.

character_motion_contract.clock: project timeline frames; deterministic for scrub, capture, and export
character_motion_contract.root_motion_policy: New UI and Agent authoring use in-place root motion. Authored root motion remains readable only for legacy project migration until deterministic root extraction is available.
character_motion_contract.timeline_blocks: set_animation.animation.motionBlocks authors non-overlapping catalog clips on exact inclusive frame ranges; one author request may replace the complete block list atomically.
character_motion_contract.layering: active timeline motion block -> legacy trajectory gait -> semantic pose offsets -> hand/foot IK

character_agent_contract.binding: Only kind=character objects carry an agentBinding (session_id and/or profile_id, optional role_id, mode=possess). One character holds at most one binding; several characters may bind the same Agent. Rebinding replaces the previous binding atomically under the normal revision guard, and locked characters require force:true.
character_agent_contract.identity: DSH harness sessions reach this tool with session_id dsh-<harness session id>; the Director MCP server uses DIRECTOR_MCP_SESSION_ID. Bind the exact session_id that will drive the character, or bind a profile_id before a live session exists. The HTTP tool envelope also accepts an optional profile_id next to session_id: a binding that names a session_id is possessed only by that exact session, while a binding that names only a profile_id is possessed by any call presenting the same profile_id. The DSH plugin forwards DIRECTOR_AGENT_PROFILE_ID and the Director MCP server forwards DIRECTOR_MCP_PROFILE_ID as that envelope profile_id when set.
character_agent_contract.control: A bound Agent drives its character with the existing actions: set_character_motion, set_character_pose_controls, set_character_ik (+clear variants), update_object transform patches, set_animation, and the spatial actions place_relative/orient_toward (anchor_id/target_id are read-only references and may name any object, so a possessed character can walk up to or turn toward someone else). There is no separate movement API.
character_agent_contract.possession_scope: When the caller (session_id, or envelope profile_id for profile-only bindings) is bound to characters with mode=possess, the gateway limits that caller's workbench mutations to those characters: only character-scoped author actions (update_object, batch_update_objects, reset_transforms, align_objects, distribute_objects, focus_objects, set_object_pivot, set_object_interaction/clear_object_interaction, character pose/motion/IK actions, object-targeted set_animation/apply_animation_recipe, bind/unbind_character_agent) whose every mutated target id is a possessed character are dispatched. Spatial actions are scoped by the objects they move: place_relative/orient_toward by object_id (anchor_id and target_id stay unrestricted read-only references), arrange_group/arrange_facing_pair by every object_ids entry, and compose_blocking only when its whole character set is a subset of the possessed set. Stage-wide mutations (start_scene, replace_project, patch, undo, run_macro, correct, delete_objects, production edits, storyboard artifacts, generated_3d promotion) are rejected with a readable error. Sessions that possess no character keep full stage-wide authoring, and reads plus durable generation/transcription job commands stay available to everyone.
character_agent_contract.explicit_object_id: Explicit ids remain canonical. When the caller possesses exactly one character, character-scoped author actions may omit their object target (object_id, single-id object_ids, or object-targeted target_id) and the gateway preflight fills the possessed character id before validation. Callers possessing several characters must name the target explicitly (omission is rejected with possession_target_ambiguous), and unpossessed sessions always require explicit ids.

catalog_contract.project_asset_discovery: project_assets lists the open project's own model assets (user uploads, AI-generated promotions, and already-imported library models) instead of the packaged catalog.
catalog_contract.project_asset_authoring: Each project_assets result carries one prepared add_object action that references the existing asset_id; no upsert_asset is needed because the asset already exists in the project.
catalog_contract.discovery: Search assets before authoring. Reuse returned authoring.actions or asset objects and motion ids exactly; never invent local URLs, asset ids, or clip ids. Do not substitute Stage primitives for a missing catalog hit when blender_native can model the piece.
catalog_contract.asset_authoring: Each assets result contains a validated asset and a two-action authoring payload (upsert_asset then add_object).
catalog_contract.asset_preview: ready=image cover is packaged; runtime=render source_model_url in the shared model preview; fallback=no renderable cover is available.
catalog_contract.character_asset_authoring: Use one atomic author batch: upsert_asset with the returned asset, then add_object with kind:'character' and asset_id set to that asset id.

revision_guard.recommended: Pass the latest project_revision only when stale-edit detection matters for the requested operation.
revision_guard.unconditional: unconditional:true intentionally skips an optional stale-edit check.

execution: Author actions and patches use the normal schemas, apply as one undoable change, and report real runtime errors.
